A **Harness** is what makes a [Knowledge Graph](knowledge-graph.html) usable: it
renders the graph, serves an interface over it, and supplies the Skills,
Workflows and Tools an Agent works the graph with. The Knowledge Graph says what is
true; the Harness is how anybody reaches it.

Four words carry this page, and each means one thing only (cat-harness#1138):

| word | means | never means |
|---|---|---|
| **instance** | a node of some node kind: a workflow instance, a bean, a document-kind record | a repository |
| **Harness** | one node kind: something that renders a graph and supplies Skills, Workflows and Tools for it | a repository as such |
| **layer** | a repository in the stack, declared by its `<name>.json` and ordered by `needs` | an instance |
| **instantiated harness** | a Harness that a layer's `index.config.json` names as instantiated there | a layer that is merely mounted |

In WHO SMART content, L1 to L5 are **knowledge layers**, layers of guideline
knowledge. A layer on this page is always a repository, never a knowledge layer.

A checkout holds several layers. They stack, bottom to top — `bootstrap`, then
`cat-harness`, then the content core, then `folio-assistant` — and each
inherits what the ones below it declare. Some layers define a Harness
(`cat-harness` is one); others hold content and instantiate a Harness defined
by a layer below them, such as an implementation guide instantiating the
Harness of the guide base it builds on. That
stacking is the subject of this page, along with the two things a Harness owes
anything it takes charge of.

**The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY are used here as
[RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) defines them**, and only in
upper case, per [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). Where a
requirement below is **not yet enforced by a gate**, this page says so at the
requirement, because a conformance statement a reader cannot tell from a
description of existing behaviour misleads either way.

## Instantiation — named in the index
{: #instantiation data-fa-label="sec:the-harness-instantiation" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-harness/instantiation.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-harness/instantiation.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-harness/instantiation.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="instantiation.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/instantiation.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="instantiation.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/instantiation.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

A Harness is **instantiated** on a layer when that layer's `index.config.json`
names it. The index is the one file that says which harnesses are instantiated
here, as opposed to which layers are merely mounted for their content:

```
index.config.json       which harnesses are instantiated HERE, and where each layer comes from
<stub>.config.json      how one instantiated harness is configured
<stub>.json             what a layer DECLARES — its directories and assets
```

Three files, three questions, and three filenames: two schemas and two readers
behind one spelling is a distinction a reader would have to already know.

**Not yet what the schema says.** Today `index.config.json` has one list,
`instances[]`, and it does double duty: it says where every mounted layer comes
from, and every name in it is read as an instantiated harness
(`instantiatedHarnessNames` returns the whole list). So a content layer whose
index lists nine layers, itself and `bootstrap` included, has all nine counted
as instantiated harnesses.
Splitting the list into the harnesses instantiated here and the layers only
mounted is cat-harness#1138 phase P2. A layer with no `index.config.json` falls
back to the older rule: a root `<name>.config.json` instantiates that harness,
and a layer that declares directories but carries no config is a dependency,
inherited by whoever depends on it, with no interface of its own.

An instantiated Harness **MUST** own the visualisation published at
`<baseurl>/<stub>`. The stem every published artefact is named with is computed
in exactly one place — `artefactStub`, which returns the declared `stub` when
there is one and the `name` otherwise — so the site build, the Knowledge Graph
export and any future artefact cannot disagree about what a layer is called.

> **The stub is intended to be free of the definition's name.** A Harness
> *defined* as `folio-assistant` should be instantiable as
> `my-folio-assistant.config.json`, with the config pointing at the definition,
> and `<baseurl>/my-folio-assistant` then live. **That is not what the code
> does today** — see the last section. It is stated here because the rest of
> this page assumes it; a reader who tries it is stopped by a gate, not a
> schema.

## How the dependency tree is walked
{: #the-dependency-walk data-fa-label="sec:the-harness-the-dependency-walk" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-harness/the-dependency-walk.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-harness/the-dependency-walk.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-harness/the-dependency-walk.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="the-dependency-walk.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/the-dependency-walk.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="the-dependency-walk.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/the-dependency-walk.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

### Bottom-up, from the bootstrap

The stack is walked **from the lowest layer up**, and each layer overlays
what the ones beneath it declared. A Skill, a Voice or a directory contributed
low is visible everywhere above it; one contributed high is visible only there.
Where two layers contribute the same name, **the root wins** — it is resolved
last precisely so that it can.

The order is **declared, not computed**, in each layer's `needs` array:

```json
{ "name": "<content-core>", "needs": ["bootstrap", "cat-harness"] }
```

It is declared so that no consumer has to hardcode the layer names.

`needs` is **OPTIONAL**, and an absent value means *undetermined* rather than
*needs nothing*. `[]` is a layer asserting
it sits on nothing, which is true of exactly one layer here, while absent is
nobody having said. A consumer treating absent as `[]` would place every
unlabelled layer on the floor beside the bootstrap. Names are used rather
than paths, because a layer is identified by its `name` everywhere else and
a path breaks the moment a directory moves.

### Three relations, and they are not interchangeable

Between repositories — as opposed to between layers in one checkout — the
[Knowledge Graph page](knowledge-graph.html#repositories) sets out three relations, and a fourth, **associated**, needs no order at all. Each has its
own carrier here:

| relation | runs | carried by |
|---|---|---|
| **depends** | Content → Content | `needs` — the layer stack, foundation first |
| **references** | Tool → Content, Test → Content | `remoteGraphs` — a graph this layer knows about and does not hold |
| **utilizes** | Tool → Tool, Test → Tool, App → Content | `dependencies` in the config — what this layer USES, overlaid |
| **associated** | Content ↔ Content, any harness | `associatedHarnesses` — a harness this one knows, and where it is published; never loaded or materialized (skill `associate-harness`) |

**Only `depends` fixes an order**, so only `depends` can have a cycle in it,
and a cycle there is a defect rather than a shape. A Tool repository
*references* a Content repository without sitting above or below it; a consumer
application *utilizes* a Content repository it may depend on not at all. That
is why a consumer needs all three and collapsing them loses the distinction:
"what must be built first", "what do I know exists", and "what do I read at run
time" are three questions with three answers.

### The bootstrap is the exception, and the floor rises

`bootstrap` sits at the bottom and does not render. It is the navigation
footer; what it owes instead is its own `.json` and `.jsonld` — *"that is its
existence"*. The rendering obligation is a **floor that rises**: it starts at
`cat-harness`, which is obliged because it supplies the layers above it with
`folio/`. A layer below that floor declares its exemption in
`renderExemption` rather than being silently excused, so the exemption is a
statement somebody made and not a gap somebody left.

## What harnessing a directory obliges
{: #harnessing-a-directory data-fa-label="sec:the-harness-harnessing-a-directory" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-harness/harnessing-a-directory.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-harness/harnessing-a-directory.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-harness/harnessing-a-directory.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="harnessing-a-directory.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/harnessing-a-directory.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="harnessing-a-directory.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/harnessing-a-directory.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

A Harness does not only *hold* directories. It **harnesses** them — and a
datastore such as a git repository is harnessed the same way, **through
Tools**: the Harness names the Skills that reach the store, and a Tool supplies
the mechanism. That indirection is what lets the same Harness be driven against
a different store without rewriting a Skill.

**Declaring a directory is a promise.** It says this layer holds a graph of
that kind and a consumer may scan it, and the obligations below are what make
the promise keepable. They are stated in full by
[`harness-requirements`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/harness-requirements.html' | relative_url }})
and measured by `check:subgraph-coverage`.

| obligation | declared as | the question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| **serialisations** | `coverage.serialisations` | is each node addressable as `json`, `jsonld` and `schema.json`? |
| **visualiser** | `coverage.visualiser` | can a person LOOK at this? |
| **docs** | `coverage.docs` | can a person READ ABOUT this? |
| **skill** | `coverage.skill` | is an agent handed something that GOVERNS this? |

The first four are per declared directory. A fifth, a starting README, is per
layer and is ranked harder still: without one a reader cannot enter the
layer.

### `coverage.process` is DECLARED and is not an obligation

A directory may also name the BPMN process that **governs** it —
`coverage.process`, a diagram's basename such as `document-ingestion`. The
generated subgraph README then draws that diagram, links its `.bpmn` source and
lists the subprocesses it calls, so the page a reader lands on says how the
directory is worked rather than only what is in it.

It sits apart from the four above in two ways.

**It is not owed.** Most directories are not the subject of a process, so an
absent `coverage.process` means NOT DECLARED and never "no process" — the same
third state `readOnly` keeps — and a directory declaring none gets no such
section and is not a finding. What *is* a finding, ranked major, is a declared
name that resolves to no diagram: somebody said, and what they said points at
nothing. There is no `exempt.process`: declaring nothing already says it.

**It is declared rather than inferred** from a diagram's event names. An
event's name is editorial text, so rewording it would silently unlink the page,
and a diagram touches several directories while being *about* one —
`document-ingestion` reads `uploads/` and writes `library/`.

### The serialisation is the one obligation a Harness MAY NOT waive

A Harness **MUST** serve `json`, `jsonld` and `schema.json` at a harnessed
directory's own URL and at every node beneath it, and **MUST NOT** be excused
it. `coverage.exempt` carries three keys — `visualiser`, `docs`, `skill` — and
deliberately not a fourth, and the coverage check ranks a missing serialisation
as an unmet obligation with no by-kind test at all.

`bootstrap` is excused a visualiser because its `json` and `jsonld` *are its
existence*, so the serialisation cannot itself be excusable, or the exemption
would excuse everything. **The visualiser
is the courtesy; the serialisation is the existence claim.**

A Harness **SHOULD** provide a visualisation, and which kinds owe one is a
question about the kind rather than a blanket rule: an active state directory
in the repository root — `beans/`, `todos/`, `fsh-guts/` — owes one because a
Harness renders something for each state directory it initialises, while a kind
that was never going to need one is not carrying a debt.

That difference is why the coverage axis ranks findings **major** and **minor**
rather than counting them: major is an obligation this kind owes and the
layer has not met; minor is nobody having said yet, for a kind that never
owed one. A single count would rank `beans/` having no viewer alongside a kind
that never needed one.

A Harness **SHOULD** also carry a `docs/` directory documenting itself, and
every Harness **SHOULD** have one. `cat-harness` renders its own through the
plain documentation path — no extensions, no JavaScript where it can be avoided
— which is why it is the one layer that owns a renderable kind at all: **a
layer owns the kinds it can render.**

## Three things the model asks for and the code does not do
{: #not-declared-yet data-fa-label="sec:the-harness-not-declared-yet" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-harness/not-declared-yet.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-harness/not-declared-yet.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-harness/not-declared-yet.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="not-declared-yet.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/not-declared-yet.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="not-declared-yet.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/not-declared-yet.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Two parts of the model above are intended and **not implemented**. Each says
what a reader will actually hit, because a page that described them as working
would send somebody to look for code that is not there.

### 1. Harness is not yet a node kind

Harness is intended to be **one node kind**, and an instantiated harness an
instance of it (cat-harness#1138 phase P2). Nothing in the schemas registers
that kind today: a layer declares a `name`, directories, assets and `needs`, and what makes it
a Harness rather than a dependency is the presence of a config file, which is a
fact about the filesystem rather than a declared type.

Without a kind there is nowhere to say what a
Harness of a given sort **MUST** supply, so every obligation on this page is
prose rather than something a declaration can be validated against.

### 2. The stub is NOT free of the definition's name

The model says a Harness defined as `folio-assistant` **MAY** be instantiated
as `my-folio-assistant.config.json`, with the config pointing at the
definition. Three places refuse it, and they refuse it consistently:

- `instanceConfigFilename` **composes** the filename from the declared name,
  so the stub is derived rather than chosen.
- The left-hand navigation tests for `<declared name>.config.json` when
  deciding whether a harness is instantiated on a layer — a differently-named config
  would leave the layer with no tile.
- `check:instance-config` reports a config whose filename does not match its
  layer's name as a finding, reading it as a rename half-done.

And the config carries **no field pointing at a definition**, so even were the
filename freed there is nothing for it to point with. Freeing the stub means
adding that pointer first; the filename rule is the symptom.

---

Neither item blocks the other. Instantiation works, the dependency
walk works, and all four coverage obligations are carried and checked. What is
missing is the part that would let a Harness be **validated as** a Harness
rather than recognised as one.

## Where the rules live
{: #where-the-rules-live data-fa-label="sec:the-harness-where-the-rules-live" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-harness/where-the-rules-live.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-harness/where-the-rules-live.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-harness/where-the-rules-live.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="where-the-rules-live.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/where-the-rules-live.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="where-the-rules-live.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/where-the-rules-live.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/concepts-harness/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

As with every page here: the discipline is in the Skills, and where a Skill and
this page disagree, **the Skill wins and this page is wrong**.

| question | where it is answered |
|---|---|
| What the Knowledge Graph is, and which way its references run | [The Knowledge Graph](knowledge-graph.html) |
| How a layer declares its directories, and every graph typology | [`directory-conventions`]({{ site.baseurl }}/reference/skill-instructions/directory-conventions.html) |
| What a visualiser owes a declared directory | [Subgraph viewers](subgraph-viewers.html) |
| What a Skill states and what a Tool supplies | [`skills-and-tools`]({{ site.baseurl }}/reference/skill-instructions/skills-and-tools.html) |
| Why a tile belongs to the Harness rather than to a node | [`harness-tiles`]({{ site.baseurl }}/reference/skill-instructions/harness-tiles.html) |
| Context Overlays, and how an Agent's conditions are set | [Managing agent context](../guides/managing-agent-context.html) |

The declaration schema, including `needs`, `remoteGraphs`, `renderExemption`
and `coverage`, is
[`schemas/cat-harness.ts`](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/cat-harness/schemas/cat-harness.ts);
the config schema, including `dependencies`, is
[`schemas/harness-config.ts`](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/cat-harness/schemas/harness-config.ts).
